steps.title: Import React from 'react'
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and available for use in your component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React. This gives you access to JSX and React's component features.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing React specifically from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to write an import statement that brings React from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Define the Card component function
steps.instruction: Define a function component named Card that returns null for now. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Create a component function that takes no props and returns null. For example: function Card() { return null; }
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Define the Card component function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component function is defined that returns null.
successCriteria: The code defines a component named Card (either as function Card() or const Card = () =>) that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Card component function. This is the foundation we'll build upon.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named Card that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named Card that returns null.

steps.title: Define CardProps interface for type safety
steps.instruction: Create an interface called CardProps above your Card component function. This interface should define two required string properties: 'title' and 'description'.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can define an interface using the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CardProps interface with typed properties that will be used to define the component's props in the next step.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CardProps interface with proper TypeScript typing for the title and description props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface is named 'CardProps' and includes both 'title' and 'description' properties with the 'string' type.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create an interface named 'CardProps' with two string properties: 'title' and 'description'.

steps.title: Add CardProps type to component
steps.instruction: Add the CardProps interface as the type for the Card component's props parameter.
steps.hint: Update the Card function signature to accept props of type CardProps.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component function signature now includes typed props: `function Card(props: CardProps)`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully typed the Card component's props with the CardProps interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure to add `props: CardProps` as the parameter type in the Card function signature.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component still needs typed props. Add `props: CardProps` as the parameter.

steps.title: Add a title heading element
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div, add an h2 element to display the card's title. Use the title prop from CardProps.
steps.hint: Remember to access the title prop that was added to the component in step 4. The h2 element should be placed inside the opening and closing div tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The card component will have an h2 element inside the wrapper div that displays the title prop value.
successCriteria: h2 element is present inside the div
h2 element displays the title prop value using JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an h2 element that displays the card title. This creates a clear semantic structure for your card component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the title prop correctly. The h2 element should display the title value using curly braces like {title}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h2 element for the title is missing or not properly implemented. Check that you've added an h2 tag inside the div and that it displays the title prop value.

steps.title: Display the title prop in the heading
steps.instruction: Inside the h2 element, display the value of the title prop.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} to embed the title prop value within the h2 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h2 element will show the dynamic title passed to the Card component.
successCriteria: The h2 element contains the title prop value using curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the title prop inside the h2 element. This makes the card's title dynamic based on the prop value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the title prop inside the h2 element with curly braces {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h2 element should display the title prop value. Use curly braces {} to embed the prop value in JSX.
